subject: Private Backup/Restore: top customer asks + proposed commitments + roadmap alignment (FinBank / MedData)
thread_body:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@finbank.com>, James Wu <james.wu@finbank.com>, Nina Alvarez <nina.alvarez@meddata-systems.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@meddata-systems.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Private Backup/Restore: top customer asks + proposed commitments + roadmap alignment (FinBank / MedData)

All — following up after last week’s FinBank deep dive (DR/ops) and the MedData security review.

I’m sharing (a) the top asks we’re hearing consistently, (b) what we can credibly commit to in the first supported iteration, and (c) how that maps to our Private roadmap so we can set expectations with customers and avoid over-promising.

Attachment: Private-Backup-Restore-Customer-Asks-v0.3.pdf
Attachment: Private-Day2-BackupRestore-Roadmap-Alignment-2025Q1Q2.pptx

---
A) Top customer asks (summary)

1) Deterministic backup/restore with clear “what’s in scope”
- Control plane state: configuration DB, tenant config, routing policies, model pins/versioning metadata, authn/z integrations, and installer/Helm release configuration.
- Kubernetes dependencies: reproducible manifests/Helm values capture; guidance on when/how to use etcd snapshots.
- Explicitly called out: “Don’t tell us to back up the whole cluster and hope.”

2) DR targets they want us to design against
- FinBank: RPO ≤ 30 min (stretch goal 15 min), RTO ≤ 2 hours for control plane availability in-region restore; multi-AZ preferred.
- MedData (on-prem / constrained): RPO 4–8 hours acceptable, RTO same-day, but requires offline repeatability and evidence (audit trail).

3) Encryption + key management (no exceptions)
- Encryption at rest for backup artifacts.
- Prefer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys (cloud KMS in VPC; HSM/KMS-equivalent for on-prem where possible).
- Clear behavior when KMS is down (fail closed vs degrade) and key rotation story.

4) Air-gapped/offline installs (MedData is the forcing function)
- Signed artifacts, checksum manifests, deterministic bundle layout.
- No external calls during backup/restore.
- Offline docs/runbooks shipped with the bundle.

5) “Prove it works” and “make it operable”
- Post-restore validation: automated smoke test that checks key APIs/routes, tenant config, and that the control plane is healthy.
- Observability: last backup success timestamp, duration, bytes, failure reason, and alerting thresholds.
- A supported DR runbook + cadence for restore drills (staging/periodic).

6) Supported storage backends
- VPC: S3 + KMS is the default ask.
- On-prem: NFS is the common ask (plus “please give us guardrails for permissions/mount opts”).

---
B) Proposed commitments (what we should say externally)

What we WILL support in v1 (supported + documented):
- A control-plane backup/restore workflow via the Private installer tooling (CLI-driven), producing:
  - A manifest (versioned; includes component inventory + checksums)
  - An encrypted artifact (tarball) containing control-plane state export + Helm values capture
- Storage backends:
  - S3 (with KMS) for VPC deployments
  - NFS target for on-prem deployments
- Restore validation:
  - A standard “post-restore validation report” (CLI output + JSON) that Support/Solutions can use.
- Runbooks:
  - Step-by-step backup and restore runbooks (including abort criteria and rollback guidance)
  - DR plans for: single-region VPC restore into clean cluster; on-prem/air-gapped flow
- Observability:
  - Metrics + dashboards for backup job success, duration, bytes, last_success_ts, and restore drill results

What we will NOT claim in v1 (explicitly out of scope):
- Backing up data plane caches / model weights / customer application data (we’ll provide guidance on stateless redeploy patterns)
- One-click cross-region DR orchestration (we can provide guidance + templates, but it’s not “push button” in the first release)
- “Kubernetes cluster backup as a product” (we’ll integrate with common tools like Velero where it makes sense, but we won’t own full-cluster recovery)

---
C) Timeline alignment (for expectation setting)

Assuming we keep focus tight:
- Phase 0 (now through mid-Feb): requirements + threat model + RPO/RTO targets per archetype; confirm supported backends and key mgmt approach
- Phase 1 (late Feb–Mar): implement core backup + restore in installer; draft runbooks; artifact format/versioning
- Phase 2 (Mar–Apr): Helm/Terraform hooks + dashboards/alerts; restore validation tooling; staging DR rehearsals
- Phase 3 (late Apr–May): game day + hardening; docs final; release checklist + support enablement

Markus/Aisha: can you reply-all with any corrections to the above before we use it as the baseline in customer comms this week?

Sarah/James/Nina/Priya: if the above commitments match your expectations, we’ll also propose a short working session to validate your target architecture (and ensure we’re aligned on RPO/RTO assumptions).

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Product, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

This matches what I’m hearing.

Two FinBank-specific clarifications I’d add (so we don’t get stuck in procurement later):

1) Restore target: they want the “restore into a clean cluster in the same region” path to be the primary supported DR story for phase 1. Cross-region is desired but can be a follow-on.

2) Evidence: their risk team asked for two things explicitly:
- A log/audit trail of backup job runs (success/failure + who invoked it)
- A “restore drill record” they can attach to their internal DR attestation

Sarah/James: if you want, I can send a draft Mutual Action Plan update based on Vivek’s timeline.

Markus Klein

Subject: Re: Private Backup/Restore: top customer asks + proposed commitments + roadmap alignment (FinBank / MedData)

+1 overall.

Security notes to bake into the external wording (so we don’t end up with ambiguity):

- “Encrypted at rest” should be described as: backup artifacts are encrypted prior to writing to the backend, using envelope encryption. For cloud deployments we’ll support KMS-managed wrapping keys; for on-prem we’ll support a pluggable provider interface (customer-provided key service/HSM integration is common).

- Secrets: we should be explicit that we are not exporting raw secret material by default. Backups include references/identifiers to secrets in the customer’s secret manager, and restore validates presence/permissions. (If a customer requests “include secrets,” that becomes a separate risk review / exception path.)

- Key rotation: we can say we support rotation by re-wrapping the data key (no need to re-encrypt payload) where the provider supports it; details depend on environment.

- Failure mode: if KMS/key provider is unavailable, backup should fail closed (no unencrypted artifacts).

If you want a single paragraph you can paste into emails/handouts, I can draft today.

Aisha Rahman
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private Backup/Restore: top customer asks + proposed commitments + roadmap alignment (FinBank / MedData)

Vivek — thanks, this is helpful.

The commitments you outlined for v1 are aligned with what we need for initial rollout, assuming:

- We can run scheduled backups (CronJob or equivalent) with clear success/failure reporting.
- Restore instructions are explicit about prerequisites and ordering. We’ve been burned by “restore DB then deploy” docs that omit CRDs/Helm ordering.
- We can demonstrate a restore drill in a non-prod environment prior to signing off.

We’re fine treating cross-region DR as a phase 2/3 discussion.

Happy to do the working session. James can share our current target topology (single region, multi-AZ) and our constraints around IAM.

Sarah Patel
Director, Infrastructure Platform
FinBank


From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@finbank.com>, Nina Alvarez <nina.alvarez@meddata-systems.com>

Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 4:48 PM PST
Subject: Re: Private Backup/Restore: top customer asks + proposed commitments + roadmap alignment (FinBank / MedData)

Sarah — confirmed on all three points.

On scheduling: we plan to support both:
1) operator-invoked backups via the installer CLI (for ad-hoc)
2) an optional scheduled path (Kubernetes CronJob) with retries/resource limits and metrics for success/failure

On ordering: we’ll make prerequisites explicit (CRDs/Helm releases/control plane bootstrap sequence) and include an “abort/rollback” section. We’ll also add a pre-flight check in the restore workflow that fails early if required CRDs or dependencies are missing.

Proposed next steps (FinBank):
- 60 min working session this week (Markus to coordinate) to confirm:
  - RPO/RTO targets and restore destination (clean cluster in same region)
  - storage backend (S3 + KMS) + IAM least-privilege policy shape
  - what constitutes “restore validation” for your sign-off

Nina/Priya — we’ll follow up separately to confirm the on-prem/offline constraints and the signed bundle requirements (and what your security team needs as evidence for retention/audit).

Thanks all. We’ll use this thread as the baseline for written commitments and keep you posted as we lock the ADR and the first draft runbooks.

Vivek
